housing: Cannock Chase is a former coalfield district, and many homes are miners' terraces and post-war estates in Cannock, Hednesford, Chadsmoor and Norton Canes. Rugeley has a market-town centre and large new-build areas, including homes on the site of the old power station. Private renting is lower than the national average, at about one in six households, and most lets are terraced houses and semis rather than flats. The district takes its name from the Cannock Chase forest and heathland to the north.
checkinTips: Former miners' terraces in Hednesford and Chadsmoor: photograph back yards, rear gates, outbuildings and any cracking to walls or ceilings.
Post-war semis on the estates: record the boiler, any storage heaters and the condition of replacement windows and doors.
New-build homes in Rugeley and on the district's edges: note snagging marks, sealant around baths and showers and the state of new turf and fences.
Homes backing onto Cannock Chase woodland: photograph gardens, fences and gutters for leaf build-up and any damage from trees.
Flats over shops in Cannock and Rugeley town centres: check the separate entrance, the fire alarm, stair lighting and the number of keys handed over.
Driveways and garages on family estates: photograph the condition of drives, garage doors and any items left in garages or sheds.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a privately rented home can contact Cannock Chase District Council's private sector housing team, part of its environmental health service.
